stem: The student wants to contrast how fully the two programs covered their eligible populations, identifying each program by its delivery method. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• In 2023, two neighboring counties offered free blood-pressure screenings to adults.
• Harlan County sent mobile clinics to workplaces.
• Harlan's program screened 6,200 adults, or 31% of the county's eligible adults.
• Reyes County set up booths inside pharmacies.
• Reyes's program screened 9,800 adults, or 14% of the county's eligible adults.
• In Harlan, 22% of screened adults were referred for follow-up care; in Reyes, 27% were.
choices: Reyes County's pharmacy booths screened 9,800 adults in 2023, whereas Harlan County's mobile workplace clinics screened only 6,200 adults.
Harlan County's mobile workplace clinics screened 31% of the county's eligible adults, whereas Reyes County's pharmacy booths screened only 14%.
In 2023, Harlan County screened 31% of its eligible adults for high blood pressure, whereas Reyes County screened only 14% of its own.
Of adults screened at Reyes County's pharmacy booths, 27% were referred for follow-up care, compared with 22% at Harlan's mobile clinics.
explanation: The goal has two conditions. First, it limits the contrast to how fully each program covered its eligible population. That is a share of eligible adults (31% versus 14%), not a headcount. Second, it asks you to identify each program by its delivery method (mobile workplace clinics, pharmacy booths). Only B does both: it names both programs by method and sets their coverage shares side by side with 'whereas.'

A.why: You saw that the goal is about reach and grabbed the choice that contrasts how many people were screened. Raw counts don't measure how fully a program covered its eligible population. Reyes screened more people but covered a far smaller share. This choice contrasts the wrong measure, so it points the comparison the wrong way.

C.why: You found the right attribute (share of eligible adults) and stopped there. The goal also asks you to identify each program by its delivery method, and this choice never mentions mobile clinics or pharmacy booths. It meets one of the goal's two conditions.

D.why: This choice names both programs by method and marks a contrast, but it contrasts referral rates, an attribute the goal never asked about. Referral rates describe what happened to people after screening, not how fully each program covered its eligible population.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a disadvantage of aerogel relative to mineral wool when the two materials provide the same insulating value. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Engineers compared two insulating materials for exterior walls: silica aerogel blanket and mineral wool.
• Aerogel blocks heat flow better than mineral wool does.
• To match the insulating value of a 1 cm aerogel blanket, a mineral wool layer must be about 2.5 cm thick.
• A 1 cm aerogel blanket costs about $40 per square meter; a 2.5 cm mineral wool layer costs about $5.
• Aerogel is brittle and sheds dust when cut.
• Mineral wool loses much of its insulating value when wet.
choices: For the same insulating value, an aerogel blanket needs to be only 1 cm thick, whereas a mineral wool layer must be about 2.5 cm thick.
For the same insulating value, an aerogel blanket costs about $40 per square meter, whereas a mineral wool layer costs only about $5.
Aerogel is brittle and sheds dust when it is cut, whereas mineral wool loses much of its insulating value when it gets wet.
An aerogel blanket is brittle and sheds dust when cut, and a 1 cm layer of it costs about $40 per square meter of wall.
explanation: The goal stacks three conditions. You need a disadvantage, not an advantage. It has to be aerogel's disadvantage relative to mineral wool, so both materials must appear with aerogel coming out worse. And the comparison has to hold at the same insulating value. B meets all three: at matched insulating value (1 cm aerogel versus 2.5 cm mineral wool), aerogel costs about $40 per square meter and mineral wool about $5. 'Whereas' and 'only' mark aerogel as the worse option.

A.why: You caught the 'same insulating value' condition and found the choice that compares the materials on that basis. But this comparison favors aerogel, since it does the job in less than half the thickness. The goal asked for a disadvantage, and this is an advantage.

C.why: This choice names both materials, gives each a drawback, and links them with 'whereas,' so it looks like a comparison of disadvantages. But it sets one drawback of each side by side instead of showing aerogel doing worse than mineral wool on a shared attribute. It also ignores the 'same insulating value' condition, and mineral wool's drawback could easily seem the more serious one.

D.why: Everything here is a disadvantage of aerogel, but mineral wool never appears, so nothing is shown relative to it. A $40 price means nothing as a drawback until you set it against mineral wool's $5 for the same insulation.
